## Weremantis Guard (Hybrid Form) (CR 3)

N Medium humanoid (human, shapechanger)  
**Init** +0; **Senses** low-light vision, scent; Perception +7  


**Defense**


**AC** 16, touch 11, flat-footed 15 (+1 Dex, +5 natural)  
**hp** 13 (1d6+1d8+4)  
**Fort** +4, **Ref** +1, **Will** +4  
**Defensive Abilities** DR 5/silver  


**Offense**


**Speed** 30 ft.  
**Melee** pitchfork (spear) +2 (1d8+2), club +2 (1d6+2), knife +2 (1d4+2), or 2 claws +2 (1d6+2 plus grab)  
**Ranged** club +1 (1d6+2); unlikely to throw knife for fear of losing it  
**Special Attacks** lunge, mandibles (–4 bite, 1d6 –1), sudden strike  


**Statistics**


**Str** 14, **Dex** 13, **Con** 14, **Int** 10, **Wis** 15, **Cha** 11  
**Base Atk** +1; **CMB** +4 CMD 15  
**Feats** Animal Affinity, Skill Focus (Profession [farmer])  
**Skills** Craft (carpentry) +5, Handle Animal +5, Heal +6, Knowledge (local) +4, Knowledge (nature) +4, Perception +7, Profession (farmer) +10, Ride +8, Stealth +5 (+13 in forests); Racial Modifiers +4 Perception, +4 Stealth (+12 in forests)  
**Languages** Common  
**SQ** change shape (human, hybrid, and giant mantis; polymorph), inhuman appearance, lycanthropic empathy (mantids and giant mantids)  


**Special Abilities**


**Change Shape (Su)** Weremantids have three forms—a humanoid form, a giant mantis form, and a hybrid form. Equipment does not meld with the new form between humanoid and hybrid form, but does between those forms and giant mantis form. A kavraen (afflicted) weremantis can shift to giant mantis or hybrid form as a full-round action by making a DC 15 Constitution check, or humanoid form as a full-round action by making a DC 20 Constitution check. On nights when the full moon is visible, a kavraen weremantis gains a +5 morale bonus to Constitution checks made to assume mantis or hybrid form, but a –5 penalty to checks made to assume humanoid form. He reverts to his humanoid form automatically with the next sunrise, or after 8 hours rest, whichever comes first. A slain weremantis reverts to its humanoid form, although it remains dead.  

**Inhuman Appearance (Ex)** When a weremantis switches from humanoid to hybrid form, his body changes more than is the case for most lycanthropes. Decidedly insectoid features — such as compound eyes, spines lining his limbs, exterior mandibles outside of his humanoid mouth, antennae, bits of chitinous natural armor, even oddly-jointed extra limbs — can all appear as part of the transformation, and no two hybrid weremantids are likely to have the same array of mantis features. A weremantis in hybrid form takes a penalty of –4 on any Disguise attempts.  

**Lycanthropic Empathy (Su)** Weremantids in hybrid or giant mantis form can communicate empathically with other mantids, including both tiny and giant mantises, They cannot control or influence mindless insects, but can share information at the level of base emotions or drives: hunger, fear, mating desire, etc.  

**Lunge (Ex)** In hybrid form a weremantid’s limbs are capable of reaching much farther than normal for a creature of his size. As a full-attack action, it can make a single attack with its claws at double its normal reach. When a weremantis attacks with a claw in this manner, he gains a +4 bonus on his attack roll. A weremantis cannot make attacks of opportunity with his lunge.  

**Mandibles (Ex)** A hybrid weremantis who grabs a foe can make a bite attack against that foe as a secondary attack. The weremantid’s bite is a –4 attack that inflicts 1d6–1 points of damage on a hit.  

**Sudden Strike (Ex)** A weremantis in hybrid form is particularly adept at moving quickly when his foes are surprised. During a surprise round, a weremantis may act as if he had a full round to act, rather than just one standard action.
